title: Marathi Negative Sentences: नाही, नको & Don't
description: How to say no, not and don't in Marathi — the आहे→नाही flip and नको for “don't want”, with curriculum examples and Hindi comparison.
secondaryKeywords: how to say no in marathi
intro: Marathi negation has three everyday tools: नाही (is not / no — the opposite of आहे), नको (don't want), and नका (don't — the negative command). The grammar notes below come straight from Unit 02 of the Bol Marathi curriculum, where असणे (to be) is taught first positive, then negative.

Hindi speakers: the skeleton is familiar — आहे flips to नाही the way है flips to नहीं. The Marathi-specific parts are नको (want-negation is its own word, not नाही पाहिजे) and word-final placement in commands.
tip: Learn the pair together: पाहिजे (need/want) ↔ नको (don't want). They are used hundreds of times a day.

sections.heading: नाही — the आहे flip
paragraphs: Positive: मी तयार आहे (I am ready). Negative: मी तयार नाही. The verb-be negates in place; nothing else in the sentence moves. Unit 06 even drills the question form: कळतंय का? — नाही, कळत नाही (Understood? — No, didn’t understand).
This is the single highest-frequency transformation in spoken Marathi. Get आहे ↔ नाही automatic and half of survival Marathi opens up.

sections.heading: नको — don't want is one word
paragraphs: Hindi splits it: नहीं चाहिए. Marathi fuses it: नको. The real Unit 02 sentence मला चहा नको, पाणी द्या (no tea, give water) shows the pair in action: पाहिजे for “need”, नको for “don't want”. Saying मला चहा नाही पाहिजे is understandable but not what people say.
For telling someone not to do something, the negative imperative is नका: that form appears in Unit 02’s imperative lessons alongside polite requests.

mistakes.wrong: मला चहा नाही पाहिजे for “I don't want tea”
mistakes.why: नको is its own word — it is not assembled from नाही + पाहिजे.

mistakes.wrong: Moving नाही to the front like English “not”
mistakes.right: Keep नाही where आहे stood: मी तयार नाही
mistakes.why: Marathi negates the verb in place; the sentence order stays verb-final.

mcq.question: “I am not ready” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: आहे flips to नाही in place.

mcq.question: Which word means “don't want”?
mcq.explanation: नको = don't want; नका = don't (command); नाही = is not.

translate.source: मुझे चाय नहीं चाहिए, पानी दीजिए।
translate.note: The real Unit 02 sentence — नको carries the whole negation.

faq.question: How do you say “no” in Marathi?
faq.answer: नाही (nāhī). To negate a sentence, flip आहे to नाही: मी तयार आहे → मी तयार नाही.

faq.question: What is the difference between नको and नाही?
faq.answer: नाही negates “is” (आहे → नाही). नको means “don't want” (पाहिजे → नको). And नका means “don't” in commands.

title: Marathi Commands & Polite Requests: या, जा, द्या
description: Marathi imperatives and polite requests — या, द्या, बसा, कृपया — with curriculum examples, Hindi comparison and cultural etiquette notes.
intro: Marathi commands are short and verb-first-feeling: या (come), जा (go), खा (eat), द्या (give). Add कृपया (please) or use the polite request forms and blunt commands become courteous ones. The notes below are the verified Unit 02 imperative and polite-request lessons, plus Unit 13's cultural-etiquette note.

Hindi speakers: the roots look familiar (आइए/जाइए/खाइए → या/जा/खा), but Marathi polite forms are terser. The tune of politeness comes from कृपया placement and the honorific तुम्ही rather than long verb endings.
tip: Default to कृपया with strangers and elders; bare imperatives are for friends, children and urgency.

sections.heading: From blunt to polite
paragraphs: या! (come!) works in an emergency; कृपया इथे या (please come here) works with a stranger — the real Unit 02 sentence. बसा (sit) becomes respectful as राव, कसे आहात? कृपया बस्या from Unit 05's honorific lesson.
Festival and home etiquette (Unit 13) layers on top: greetings, taking blessings, and the softeners that keep commands sounding like invitations.

mistakes.right: Add कृपया or the honorific tone: कृपया बसा
mistakes.why: Marathi marks respect through कृपया, तुम्ही and honorific address rather than Hindi-style -इए endings alone.

mistakes.right: Use नका: इथे जाऊ नका (don't go here)
mistakes.why: नाही negates statements; नका negates commands.

mcq.question: Which word turns a blunt command into a polite request?

fill.hint: The Unit 02 sentence — imperative of येणे.

translate.note: From Unit 09 — command + कृपया, polite anywhere.

faq.question: How do you say “please” in Marathi?
faq.answer: कृपया (kr̥payā) — same word as Hindi. Place it before or after the command: कृपया इथे या / बिल द्या, कृपया.

faq.question: How do Marathi imperatives differ from Hindi?
faq.answer: Roots overlap (या/जा/खा), but Marathi polite requests are shorter; respect is carried by कृपया and the तुम्ही form instead of long -इए endings.

title: Marathi Possessives: माझा, माझी, माझं Explained
description: My, your, his in Marathi: माझा/माझी/माझं agree with the owned noun's gender — with curriculum examples and Hindi comparison.
intro: Marathi has three genders — masculine, feminine and neuter — and possessives agree with the thing owned, not the owner: माझा भाऊ (my brother), माझी बहीण (my sister), माझं पुस्तक (my book). The notes below come from Unit 02's possession lesson and Unit 03's adjective-agreement lesson.
Hindi speakers already know agreement (मेरा/मेरी); the new work is the third gender. नाव, पुस्तक, कुटुंब, पाणी are all neuter and take माझं.
tip: Learn every new noun together with its possessive: माझं पुस्तक, माझी बहीण — gender comes free that way.

sections.heading: The three-way split
paragraphs: माझा for masculine nouns, माझी for feminine, माझं for neuter. The curriculum sentences make it concrete: हे माझं पुस्तक आहे (this is my book — neuter), ही माझी बहीण आहे (this is my sister — feminine), माझं कुटुंब मोठं आहे (my family is big — neuter again).
Unit 03's adjective-agreement note extends the same logic to describing words — once possessives agree, adjectives follow the same three genders.

mistakes.why: Hindi मेरा नाम misleads: Marathi नाव takes the neuter possessive.

mistakes.wrong: Agreement with the owner instead of the noun
mistakes.right: A woman says माझा भाऊ too — the brother is masculine
mistakes.why: The possessive matches the owned thing's gender, not the speaker's — same logic as Hindi, one more gender.

fill.sentence: हे ___ पुस्तक आहे. (This is MY book.)

faq.question: How many genders does Marathi have?
faq.answer: Three: masculine, feminine and neuter — and possessives (माझा/माझी/माझं) agree with the gender of the thing owned.

faq.question: Is माझं for plural?
faq.answer: No — माझं is neuter singular. Plural possessives (माझे/माझ्या/माझीं) are covered inside Units 02–03 along with the agreement rules.
